transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-03-04 16:00 PT | Duration: 62m | Attendees: Ethan, Maya, Liam / Rachel, Tomás, Priya

Summary: short practice sprint — two live demo runs, three rapid objection rehearsals, and mapping next steps for snippet production and battlecard edits.

[00:00] Ethan: ok team, welcome thanks for joining. quick agenda: warm up, two practice demos, then competitive rebuttals and we wrap with next steps. roughly an hour.
[00:22] Rachel: yep thanks, we want practical lines we can reuse with field. also short clips for our internal enablement hub.
[00:38] Maya: got it, i'll lead the first demo — i'll try the single-tenant dedicated story first, show autoscale, then hand to Ethan for closing.
[00:50] Tomás: curious — can you call out latency numbers versus model size during the demo? our SEs always struggle with that.
[01:10] Maya: sure, i'll say typical p95 sub 250ms for chat on small-medium models on dedicated, watchers note that for longer context it increases. 
[02:05] (demo start)
[02:10] Maya: launching Redwood Console, route configured to dedicated pool -> model catalog -> selecting "redwood-rlhf-14b" (note: model label may be transcribed wrong, actual model name redwood-14b-rlhf). showing token breakdown, prefix caching on for repeated prompts.
[03:00] Maya: ok watch how autoscale policy kicks in when i crank concurrency; watch the dashboard latency spike then stabilization.
[03:22] Ethan: call out cost math here — emphasize per-token transparency, show the token counter, and compare to competitor fuzzed numbers.
[04:05] Priya: can you explain fallback — like if we hit capacity what happens?
[04:20] Maya: yes, we have smart routing + model variants, automatic fallback to smaller quantized variant, canary policy optionally, and we can route by cost or latency preference. point out: cache+batching reduces unit cost.
[05:01] Tomás: pretty good. suggestion: when you say "quantized variant" maybe give a one-liner on quality tradeoff.
[05:30] Maya: good call. i'll add: "quantized models cut token compute but may affect long-tail reasoning; we validate on eval sets first."

-- Objection rehearsal 1: Latency vs Cost (08:12) --
[08:12] Ethan: customers ask why not just use hosted cheap model. our line: hosted is fastest path to value with per-token pricing but dedicated gives predictable throughput + isolation for scale/SLAs. say: hosted for pilot, dedicated when you need predictability.
[09:00] Rachel: we need a one-line for execs on why Redwood vs Anthropic/OpenAI.
[09:18] Ethan: "Redwood focuses on serving economics — predictable latency SLOs and cost controls (batching, cache, quantization) so you can scale with fewer surprises."
[09:45] Rachel: nice, can we have a variant that calls out Private for regulated workloads?
[10:02] Maya: "When data residency/compliance matter, Private (VPC or on-prem) gives you a customer-controlled plane, KMS integration, and audit logs."

-- Objection rehearsal 2: Security/Compliance (13:30) --
[13:30] Tomás: Show the SOC2/SSO line. customers always want SAML and audit trails.
[13:45] Liam: short line: "We support SSO/SAML, RBAC, KMS/HSM integrations, and audit logs; we can retain telemetry per your retention policy or forward to your lake."
[14:05] Priya: what about airgap? we sometimes get asked.
[14:22] Maya: Private on-prem is our answer, note: there is an enterprise packaging and support plan — mention the timeline caveat up front, it's not instant.

-- Objection rehearsal 3: Competitor claim — Better model quality (18:10) --
[18:10] Ethan: if they say "Anthropic/OpenAI have better quality" response: "Model quality is important but serving is the differentiator; we provide verified performance profiles, easy rollbacks, and can route to higher-quality variants for critical paths while keeping cost-effective paths for background tasks."
[19:02] Rachel: can you show an example of routing policy?
[19:20] Maya: quick show: route by header -> users with premium flag go to high-quality model in dedicated pool; others go to cached quantized variant — demo snippet will be part of the library.

-- Second demo run & handoff (26:45) --
[26:45] Maya: this run i'll intentionally trigger a fallback to the quantized variant and show output diff. note: transcription may not capture exact model names.
[27:00] (demo runs, some crosstalk)
[30:15] Ethan: smooth handoff — remind AE to set expectations before handing to SE: "i'm going to show the business value in 90s, then Maya will demo the technical guardrails". keep handoff line short.
[31:02] Rachel: can you both repeat that handoff line? we want a 1-sentence script.
[31:10] Ethan: "We'll show how this feature reduces time-to-insight by X and lowers per-token cost via caching; Maya will show technical controls briefly."
[31:35] Maya: "I'll demonstrate configuration and show a rapid failover to a lower-cost variant while preserving availability."

-- Messaging workshop (36:00) --
[36:00] Liam: for the battlecard, we need top 3 differentiators and top 3 competitor counters. my draft: 1) Predictable economics (batching/cache), 2) Unified runtime across hosted/dedicated/private, 3) Observability + rollouts.
[36:42] Tomás: counters: to Anthropic — "we win on production economics and operational controls"; to OpenAI — "we win on dedicated capacity & private deployments"; to MosaicML — "we win on unified developer experience + drop-in rollback".
[37:15] Rachel: prefer shorter tweets for SDRs: "Fast pilot, predictable scale, private when needed."

-- Practical tips for demos (40:50) --
[40:50] Maya: top tips: 1) Start with a short value statement, 2) show Live metric (latency/cost), 3) demo a graceful failure, 4) always end with next steps.
[41:12] Ethan: also: keep token counters visible and narrate what causes token spikes — customers trust transparency.
[41:45] Priya: is there a canonical place to pull token cost estimates from?
[42:00] Liam: we'll maintain a public spreadsheet in the snippet library with the common prompts and token counts — Maya will add two canonical snippets today.

-- Quick roleplay (47:05) --
[47:05] Ethan -> Rachel (as buyer): "We need sub-200ms at scale".
[47:12] Rachel (buyer): "Can you guarantee that?"
[47:20] Ethan: "We set SLOs by pool and offer canary rollouts; for strict sub-200ms you'll want dedicated capacity and tuned kernels—Liam can run a throughput calc to show feasibility in your environment."
[48:00] (feedback)
[49:30] Maya: observed filler words in the handoff, suggest Ethan shorten to one phrase and use the scripted sentence.

-- Closing and wrap (55:10) --
[55:10] Ethan: recap: we'll produce two demo snippets, the rebuttal one-pager, and the battlecard draft. we'll also run the throughput calc and share pricing/pilot template.
[56:00] Rachel: love it — we'll review and send feedback on the battlecard by next Monday.
[56:25] Priya: small ask — can you add an executive cheat sheet for C-suite that fits on one slide?
[56:40] Ethan: yes, action item for me.
[57:05] Liam: final note for SEs — log demo variations and outcomes in the snippet library so we can iterate on the best wording.
[57:40] Tomás: thanks all, this was useful.
[58:00] (meeting ends)

References shared: link: https://redwood.internal/snippet-library (internal), battlecard draft (attached), demo-recording-1 (internal note).

Transcription notes: some product names may be partially transcribed (redwood-14b-rlhf etc), times are approximate.
